content: When enzyme inducers are used alongside combined hormonal contraceptives (CHCs), it is essential to use an alternative or backup method of contraception. This backup method should be continued for 28 days after discontinuing the enzyme inducer to maintain contraceptive reliability. Erythromycin base, ethylsuccinate, lactobionate, and stearate can reduce the levels or effectiveness of levonorgestrel/ethinyl estradiol/ferrous bisglycinate by altering intestinal flora. This interaction applies only to oral forms of the hormone and carries a low risk of contraceptive failure. Caution and monitoring are advised, as antibiotics may decrease the efficacy of hormonal contraceptives. Eslcarbazepine acetate and etravirine can decrease the levels or effectiveness of levonorgestrel/ethinyl estradiol/ferrous bisglycinate by affecting hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy should be modified, and close monitoring is recommended. The efficacy of hormonal contraceptives may be reduced, necessitating the use of alternative or backup contraception during and for 28 days after discontinuing enzyme inducers. Fosamprenavir may increase the levels or effects of levonorgestrel/ethinyl estradiol/ferrous bisglycinate by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are advised, as coadministration with CYP3A4 inhibitors can increase plasma hormone concentrations. Nonhormonal contraception is recommended. Fosaprepitant can decrease the levels or effectiveness of levonorgestrel/ethinyl estradiol/ferrous bisglycinate by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy should be modified, and close monitoring is necessary. The efficacy of hormonal contraceptives may be reduced, requiring alternative or backup contraception during and for 28 days after discontinuing enzyme inducers. Fosphenytoin and phenytoin can reduce the levels or effectiveness of levonorgestrel/ethinyl estradiol/ferrous bisglycinate by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy adjustments and close monitoring are required. Hormonal contraceptive efficacy may be compromised, necessitating alternative or backup contraception during and for 28 days after discontinuing enzyme inducers. Grapefruit can increase the levels or effects of levonorgestrel/ethinyl estradiol/ferrous bisglycinate by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are advised, as coadministration with CYP3A4 inhibitors may increase plasma hormone concentrations. Nonhormonal contraception is recommended. Griseofulvin can decrease the levels or effectiveness of levonorgestrel/ethinyl estradiol/ferrous bisglycinate by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy should be modified, and close monitoring is necessary. Hormonal contraceptive efficacy may be reduced, requiring alternative or backup contraception during and for 28 days after discontinuing enzyme inducers. Idelalisib, imatinib, isoniazid, itraconazole, and ketoconazole can increase the levels or effects of levonorgestrel/ethinyl estradiol/ferrous bisglycinate by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are advised, as coadministration with CYP3A4 inhibitors may increase plasma hormone concentrations. Nonhormonal contraception is recommended. Ivosidenib may decrease the levels or effectiveness of levonorgestrel/ethinyl estradiol/ferrous bisglycinate through an unspecified interaction mechanism. Therapy should be modified, and close monitoring is necessary. Alternative contraception methods should be considered for patients receiving ivosidenib. Lamotrigine levels may be significantly decreased when used with combined hormonal contraceptives (CHCs) containing ethinyl estradiol (EE), likely due to induction of lamotrigine glucuronidation. This interaction may reduce seizure control, necessitating dosage adjustments of lamotrigine. Levonorgestrel/ethinyl estradiol/ferrous bisglycinate may decrease the levels or effects of levothyroxine, liothyronine, or liotrix due to an unknown mechanism. The estrogen component of CHCs may increase serum concentrations of thyroxine-binding globulin, potentially requiring increased doses of thyroid hormone replacement therapy. Lixisenatide may decrease the levels or effectiveness of levonorgestrel/ethinyl estradiol/ferrous bisglycinate by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption. Oral contraceptives should be taken at least 1 hour before or 11 hours after lixisenatide administration. Lonapegsomatropin, somapacitan, somatrogon, and somatropin may have reduced effectiveness when coadministered with levonorgestrel/ethinyl estradiol/ferrous bisglycinate due to pharmacodynamic antagonism. Oral estrogens may reduce serum insulin-like growth factor I (IGF-1) response to growth hormone analogs, potentially requiring higher growth hormone doses. Lumacaftor/ivacaftor can decrease the levels or effectiveness of levonorgestrel/ethinyl estradiol/ferrous bisglycinate by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy should be modified, and close monitoring is necessary. Hormonal contraceptive efficacy may be reduced, requiring alternative or backup contraception during and for 28 days after discontinuing enzyme inducers. Metronidazole, minocycline, and other antibiotics may decrease the levels or effectiveness of levonorgestrel/ethinyl estradiol/ferrous bisglycinate by altering intestinal flora. This interaction applies only to oral forms of the hormone and carries a low risk of contraceptive failure. Caution and monitoring are advised. Mitotane, nafcillin, and other enzyme inducers can reduce the levels or effectiveness of levonorgestrel/ethinyl estradiol/ferrous bisglycinate by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy adjustments and close monitoring are required. Hormonal contraceptive efficacy may be compromised, necessitating alternative or backup contraception during and for 28 days after discontinuing enzyme inducers. Midazolam levels may be increased when coadministered with levonorgestrel/ethinyl estradiol/ferrous bisglycinate due to decreased metabolism. Caution and monitoring are advised, as ethinyl estradiol may inhibit the clearance of benzodiazepines that undergo oxidation, increasing serum concentrations. Mineral oil may decrease the levels or effectiveness of levonorgestrel/ethinyl estradiol/ferrous bisglycinate by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption. Therapy should be modified, and close monitoring is necessary. St. John’s Wort can decrease the levels or effectiveness of levonorgestrel/ethinyl estradiol/ferrous bisglycinate by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy should be modified, and close monitoring is necessary. Hormonal contraceptive efficacy may be reduced, requiring alternative or backup contraception during and for 28 days after discontinuing enzyme inducers. Sulfonamides (e.g., sulfadiazine, sulfamethoxazole, sulfisoxazole) may decrease the levels or effectiveness of levonorgestrel/ethinyl estradiol/ferrous bisglycinate by altering intestinal flora. This interaction applies only to oral forms of the hormone and carries a low risk of contraceptive failure. Caution and monitoring are advised. Temazepam levels may be decreased when coadministered with levonorgestrel/ethinyl estradiol/ferrous bisglycinate due to an unknown mechanism. Caution and monitoring are advised. Tetracycline and other antibiotics may decrease the levels or effectiveness of levonorgestrel/ethinyl estradiol/ferrous bisglycinate by altering intestinal flora. This interaction applies only to oral forms of the hormone and carries a low risk of contraceptive failure. Caution and monitoring are advised. Theophylline levels may be increased when coadministered with levonorgestrel/ethinyl estradiol/ferrous bisglycinate due to decreased metabolism. Caution and monitoring are advised, as combined oral contraceptives containing ethinyl estradiol may inhibit metabolism and increase plasma concentrations of certain drugs.
